summary: How Tech Works: watched 3 Shorts with new numbers (Motorola brick, Paris Metro, NVIDIA) and the 2 newest. Widened lesson #1 so the second line can't open on a date or backstory either, and added evidence to two challengers.
why: The second line still loses the most viewers whenever it isn't the machine working: brick -19 points at 5.5 s on backstory (stayed 47.2%, 10.4 under the 57.6% median), Paris -20.9 at 6.1 s on a date plus a re-asked question, microwave -29.6 at 7.5 s. That is three Shorts over the 15-point bar.

findings.title: A date or backstory as the second line costs 19-30 points
findings.detail: Brick 5.5 s 'Its engineers had just 6 weeks...' -19; Paris 6.1 s 'Paris first tried it in 1951. So what keeps it...' -20.9; microwave 7.5 s 'In 1945...' -29.6. NVIDIA, made after the lesson, opened line 2 on a count and lost 13.9.

findings.title: Payoff figures still counting while the voice says them
findings.detail: NVIDIA shows 297B while saying 336B, the wing 528 while saying 575 tonnes, the transistor 45B while saying 76B. This is a fix for the improver.

findings.title: Logo clipped at the frame edge
findings.detail: NVIDIA v-20261125-21 at 25 s: the Microsoft logo is cut off at the right edge. The layout gate checks text only.

findings.title: Fewer places, better hold after the hook
findings.detail: Crossrail 45.5%, Paris 35.4%, NVIDIA 31.5%, brick 29.8% (seven places). Added to the tech-one-machine-one-place test.

changes.title: Lesson #1 widened: no second question, date or backstory before the machine
Challenger evidence added
changes.detail: tech-mechanism-by-6s (now partly covered by lesson #1) and tech-one-machine-one-place.
